text: Right now, the account behind Oakmere's nightly core-banking sync can reach almost anything on the internal network -- not because anyone decided that, just because the network is flat.

Renata and the infrastructure team build a dedicated network security group with a default deny, then open exactly two narrow exceptions -- the one database it syncs to, and the one vendor it talks to.
Flow logs from that group feed straight into Sentinel, so any attempt to go anywhere else becomes a logged, queryable event instead of a silent drop.
The nightly sync still runs clean. A test connection to an unrelated internal subnet gets denied and shows up in the logs -- proof the lockdown actually holds.
Next: a pipeline pass that catches the team's own near-repeat of this exact mistake before it ever ships.
